question.text: Ms. Priya Shah, fund accountant at Aravalli Long-Short Fund (Cat III AIF, trust structure), is computing the fund-level tax liability on business income. Which effective rate does the workbook cite as the Maximum Marginal Rate (MMR) applicable to derivative (F&O) business income earned by a Category III AIF?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook explicitly states that gains from F&O transactions earned by a Category III AIF are treated as Profits and Gains from Business and Profession and that the fund is liable to pay tax on such income at the Maximum Marginal Rate of 42.744%. The Trap: 30% is the pre-surcharge base rate. 34.944% is the effective rate the workbook cites for corporate non-concessional taxation. 25.168% is the Section 115BAA concessional corporate effective rate. Only 42.744% matches the MMR figure cited in the workbook for Category III F&O business income. Note: Because there is no Section 115UB pass-through for Category III AIFs, this MMR-level tax is borne at the fund level and reduces the NAV available to investors.
